messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT (P1) detected: sudden p95 token latency spike from ~240ms -> 2.6s across us-west-2 serving nodes. Alert: <https://alerts.redwood.io/3987654321>. Paging on-call. Runbook: <https://runbooks.redwood.io/latency-regression>

alice: oncall alice here, acked. Starting triage — collecting traces and checking recent deploys. Any initial customer impact notes?

mike: telemetry: ~12% of requests >1s, error rate stable. Affected model tag: redwood/gpt-neo-1 (v2026-03). p50 shifted from ~120ms -> ~200ms. p95 2.6s. Capturing timeline now.

sam: uploading traces: https://traces.redwood.io/trace/3987654321. Early look: spike aligns with kernel scheduling jitter on 4 nodes (node01,node03,node05,node06). Dropping perf counters shortly.

kevin: please paste perf stat/top snippets if you have them. Need sample spans and callstacks.

sam: perf snippet from node01 (sample):
```
# perf top -p <pid>
cpu-clock 30.2% <kernel_task>
context-switches 48k/s
softirq 9.4%
__schedule 22%
__schedule_tail 8.1%
```
(others similar)

rachel: customer impact: three higher-tier customers reporting degraded latency: acme-co, beta-inc, shoply. CS notified and ticket INC-2321 created. Draft customer blurb ready for approval.

alice: mitigation actions: increased Dedicated pool capacity +20% (policy: emergency-scale), enabled model-variant fallback to quantized-v1 for low-latency tier. Rolling deploy started.

incident-bot: mitigation applied: autoscale +20% on pool "us-west-2-dedicated-1"; model fallback enabled for route /v1/generate. Observe p95 dropping to ~1.1s on subset after changes.

mike: logs uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/3987654321/logs.tar.gz (includes dmesg, kernel logs, trace spans). Notable dmesg lines: "sched: rq-1: runqueue length high (46)" on node01 around 12:11:36 UTC.

kevin: hypotheses: 1) kernel scheduler jitter due to unexpected softirq/irq storms (affecting runqueue). 2) interaction between recent model-loader change and thread affinity causing syscalls that exacerbate sched latency. 3) IO wait spikes from background jobs. Tagging hypotheses in-thread.

sam: kicking off cluster-wide perf stat collection:
```
for n in node{01..06}; do ssh $n "sudo perf stat -e context-switches,cycles,cache-misses -a sleep 30" >> /tmp/perf-3987.log; done
```
Will upload results to incident bucket when done.

mike: perf summary (excerpt):
```
node01: context-switches 51k, cycles 2.1e9, cache-misses 120k
node02: context-switches 12k, cycles 1.8e9, cache-misses 95k
node03: context-switches 49k, cycles 2.0e9, cache-misses 130k
```
node01/03 stand out with high context-switches.

rachel: timeline (recorded in doc): 12:04 UTC alert -> 12:06 oncall ack -> 12:10 mitigation scale+fallback -> 12:12 partial p95 improvement -> 12:18 kernel dmesg observed -> 12:25 started perf capture. Document: <https://docs.redwood.io/incidents/3987654321/timeline>

alice: handoff: @kevin taking next 10m, I'm stepping out for a customer call. Please continue trace-to-kernel correlation and update timeline. Adding hypothesis tags: [kernel_sched, io_wait, model_loader].

kevin: taking over. I'll correlate trace spans with kernel timestamps and check for eBPF or perf probes active on those nodes. If scheduler is root cause, plan: drain affected nodes one-by-one and reboot to clear state, observe p95.

customer-ops: ACME notified: "We are investigating a latency regression affecting some API requests. No data loss. Mitigation in progress. We will update every 30 minutes."

sam: found a coincident deploy at 11:58 UTC to model-loader component (canary). Rolling back the canary now to test correlation: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/model-loader-canary --namespace=prod`.

alice: back in. After rollback, canary p95 dropped to ~220ms. Canary nodes returned to normal latency. This strongly correlates the regression with the model-loader change. Updating hypothesis priority: model_loader > kernel_sched > io_wait.

kevin: updated plan: keep fallback enabled, roll back model-loader to stable on two additional canary pods (controlled), monitor p50/p95 for 30m. Collect kernel perf traces pre/post rollback: `sudo perf record -g -p <pid> -- sleep 60` and upload to s3. If rollback fixes all nodes, we'll run RCA on the model-loader diff.

incident-bot: status change: mitigated -> degraded (partial mitigation). Customer impact reduced. Next automatic update in 15 minutes. Please continue RCA and append findings to https://docs.redwood.io/incidents/3987654321/rca-draft

kevin: action items assigned in thread: [sam: full perf logs upload], [mike: kernel dmesg correlation], [alice: customer comms], [rachel: timeline + tickets], [kevin: rollback coordination and trace correlation].

mike: uploaded perf logs and callstacks to s3://redwood-incidents/3987654321/perf/. Added pointer to flamegraphs at https://telemetry.redwood.io/flame/3987654321.

alice: thanks team — we're close. If rollback continues to validate, next steps: postmortem + fix PR for model-loader to avoid syscall pattern that causes scheduler pathology.
